name: Telegram
verdict: No OAuth: you create one bot with @BotFather and use its token, with no review. Customers press Start in a DM or a group admin adds the bot, about 1-3 days.
needGuide: No — create a bot with @BotFather, store the token, and link users with a /start deep link.

auth.detail: Bot API: one token per bot from @BotFather /newbot (/token to regenerate), sent as api.telegram.org/bot<token>/. Users do not authorize the bot via OAuth; they start a chat or add it to a group. Separately, Telegram Login is now OIDC (auth code + PKCE S256, scopes openid/profile/phone/telegram:bot_access) but yields identity only. MTProto user API uses api_id/api_hash and acts as a user client.

approval.gate: None for Bot API or Login. api_id/api_hash is self-serve at my.telegram.org but unofficial clients are watched and risk bans; not suitable for connecting customers' accounts.

scopes.why: No scope model for bots; capabilities come from bot settings and admin rights.
scopes.summary: No scope model for bots: capabilities depend on bot settings (privacy mode, admin rights). Login scopes: openid, profile, phone (user consent), telegram:bot_access (lets the bot DM the user). Login grants no access to a user's chats.

prerequisites: Account and owner: A Telegram account (phone number) owns the bot in BotFather; use a company-managed account since only the owner manages tokens.
Where you register: Telegram → @BotFather → /newbot (name, username ending in bot); for login: BotFather → bot → Login Widget → add Allowed URLs → copy Client ID/Secret

registerAt.path: Telegram → @BotFather → /newbot (name, username ending in bot); for login: BotFather → bot → Login Widget → add Allowed URLs → copy Client ID/Secret

steps.do: Open @BotFather, run /newbot, choose name and username ending in bot
Store the token as a secret; rotate with /token if leaked
Set the webhook (setWebhook) or use getUpdates; handle /start with a deep-link payload to link the Telegram user to the customer account
Optional identity: BotFather → Login Widget → add Allowed URLs; implement OIDC code + PKCE and verify id_token via JWKS
Tell customer admins to add the bot to groups and set privacy mode and admin rights
Send test messages and verify webhook secret token

roles.team: A Telegram account (phone number) owns the bot in BotFather; use a company-managed account since only the owner manages tokens.
roles.console: none documented (BotFather is single-owner; managed bots can have a manager bot).
roles.customer: For group/channel use, a group admin (or channel admin) must add the bot and grant rights; end users in DMs just press Start. No workspace-admin approval exists.

testing: Create a bot in BotFather and message it from your own account; add it to a test group.
Login: add localhost or staging URLs to Allowed URLs.

blockers.problem: Users cannot connect their own account through OAuth
blockers.fix: Reading a user's own chats needs MTProto, which risks bans.

blockers.problem: Bots cannot message a user first
blockers.fix: The user must press Start (use deep links).

blockers.problem: Privacy mode hides group messages from the bot
blockers.fix: Disable it or make the bot admin.

blockers.problem: Old hash-verified Login Widget is archived

automation.agentCan: Write bot and webhook code, OIDC login code, deep-link linking, and customer setup instructions.
automation.humanMust: Telegram account and phone verification; customer group admin adds the bot.

uncertain: Bot token lifetime and limits for bots in large groups; whether Telegram plans delegated user-data OAuth (none documented).
